name: @acc/decho-components
description: The Decho component library: cards, tags, buttons, panels, nav items, an application shell, progress bars, metric tiles, dependency-free SVG charts and the rest of the pieces every operational front-end redraws. Styled from CSS custom properties with built-in fallbacks, so it looks right with no stylesheet, no provider and no dependency — and follows @acc/decho-styling's themes when they are present.
//files: src is shipped for the same two reasons as @acc/decho-styling's: source maps point at ../src/*, and the CSS entry point IS a src file — tsc copies no assets, and adding a bundler to a package whose selling point is not needing one would be a poor trade.
//peerDependencies: React is REQUIRED here, unlike in @acc/decho-styling where it is optional — a component library with an optional view layer would be a pretence. @acc/decho-styling is deliberately absent: not a dependency, not a peer, not optional-peer. The components read `var(--decho-*, <fallback>)`, so they are themed by it when it is present and correct when it is not. See README, 'Why there is no dependency on the styling package'.
//devDependencies: react-dom is for the render tests, which use renderToStaticMarkup rather than Testing Library — the same choice, for the same reason, as the styling package. @acc/decho-styling is not listed: the fallback generator and the parity test read the sibling package's source directly out of this monorepo (see scripts/gen-fallbacks.mjs), which keeps `npm install` from needing a version of it that may not be published yet.
//publishConfig: The SAME Artifacts repository as @acc/decho-styling, and not the one the five map packages use. Deliberate: a scope can only point at one registry, and tokens + components is the pair almost every consumer installs together. One registry line in a widget repo's .npmrc, not two. This URL is the public host, which does not resolve from a Code Workspace — publish from there with the --registry override documented in the root README.
